expect.note: each mutation breaks its own capability and leaves the others alone

provenance: ground-truth integrity for the whole L4 story. If a mutation silently stopped mutating — a renamed fixture element, a regex that no longer matches — every mutation case would pass for the wrong reason and the self-maintenance evidence would be worthless. Checks are literal substrings of src/browser/fixtures/shop.html. The 'getElementById: false' check was added after l4-shop-ids-renamed went red on first run (2026-08-16): the mutation was renaming ids the fixture's own script depended on, so it broke the page rather than the agent's stable-attr dependency. A fault injector that damages the fixture measures nothing. M8 added five blocks. Three claims each of them makes are checked here rather than inferred: (1) the mutation fired at all; (2) the tier the L4 case relocates TO is untouched — '>Sort by price (low to high)</button>' under duplicate-labels, the shop-rug link under a11y-stripped; (3) the mutation did not damage the fixture — 'div[type="submit"]' is the click shim without which a11y-stripped would silently disable the search form the case it guards depends on, and 'Newsletter closed' is the checkable consequence overlay-modal's dismissal leaves behind. element-reordered is the only mutation whose claim is about ORDER, so its two needles span a row boundary: rug must now precede clock, and the base order (lamp-std before lamp-pro) must be gone. render-delayed is the one mutation this file cannot fully guard — its effect happens at runtime, so only the injected script is visible as a substring; its L4 case guards the rest by expecting a failure that a dead mutation could not produce. Every other M8 case is self-guarding the same way: a dead mutation makes l4-shop-duplicate-labels, l4-shop-a11y-stripped and l4-shop-overlay-modal go RED, because each asserts the recovery (or replan) that only a live mutation forces.

triage.note: guards the fault injector, not the product
